newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mitsubishi Trust says can cope with loan losses.
newsitem.headline: Mitsubishi Trust says can cope with loan losses.

text.p: Mitsubishi Trust & Banking Corp's president said on Wednesday his company would be able to cope with losses on loans to three Nippon Credit Bank affiliates that filed for bankruptcy protection.
"The amount loaned is not small, but we will be able to deal with the losses with our operating profits for 1997/98," Toyoshi Nakano told a news conference.
Speaking of the trust bank's overall bad-loan woes, he added, "We got past the worst of our bad loan problems in our last earnings report for March 1997."
Three of NCB's non-bank financial affiliates said on Tuesday that they had filed for bankruptcy. The affiliates combined had debts estimated at more than two trillion yen.
A Japanese paper reported on Sunday that Mitsubishi Trust had made loans of 102.7 billion yen to the NCB affiliates while Sumitomo Trust & Banking Co Ltd had lent them 166 billion yen.
Nakano said the bankruptcy filing came as a surprise.
"Yesterday's announcement was really sudden and I was honestly surprised. There were things that could have been done and there should have been some talk about it," he said.
Under Japan's bankruptcy filing rules, all creditors must write off loans in proportion to the amount of loans outstanding to each affiliate.
